title: Reviewed helper wave 1 routing (Claude continuation, 2026-11-05)
description: Routing, capability-class and publication-review corrections from the model review of the DeepSeek helper-family wave (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human). They do not change source pins, package status, signatures or publication.

overrides.justification: Model review of helper wave 1: BCSMotor (bcs_motor.py:21) is a custom Ophyd positioner over a ZeroMQ client with no EPICS Components, so OphydDriver cannot bind it; LICENSE.md is the LBNL BSD form with an Enhancements grant.

Model review of helper wave 1: skip, framework: arbok builds QUA programs from user Python sequence classes and runs them on a Quantum Machines OPX (arbok_driver.py:147-155, sequence_base.py:210-228); no fixed device surface.

Model review of helper wave 1: the MCP tools are registered with mcp.add_tool, which McpClientDriver cannot prove; the card's entry symbol is the Baumer camera class (baumer_genicam.py:73), served as a direct Driver.
Model review of helper wave 1: a direct Driver over BaslerCamera; OphydDriver binds Signal get/set only and cannot publish the grabbed frame as an image artifact or bind the pylon StopGrabbing stop.

Model review of helper wave 1: SmarSignal (src/OphydSmarPod.py:65) is a custom ophyd Signal over the vendor module smaract.smarpod, which OphydDriver cannot express; a direct Driver with a native.py adapter fits.

Model review of helper wave 1: a direct Driver over RunzeSyringePump (runze_backbone.py:80), a serial syringe pump that frames /<addr><cmd>R commands (125-133); no PyLabRobot LiquidHandler front end (the LaiYu backend is a stub).
Model review of helper wave 1: NanoDrop1000 (Code/nanodrop.py:6) is a USB spectrophotometer with a binary command mailbox, not a PyLabRobot liquid handler; a direct Driver over it fits.
Model review of helper wave 1: RemoteSTARBackend is a ConnectRPC client that replaces a STARBackend (star/__init__.py:21-31), not a LiquidHandler with a deck; still blocked without a provable stop.
Model review of helper wave 1: the server dispatches a TOOLS/HANDLERS table (server.py:1327-1352), which McpClientDriver cannot prove; a direct Driver over OscilloscopeConnection (server.py:99) fits.

Model review of helper wave 1: LakeShore336 is a VisaInstrument with plain SCPI methods and no QCoDeS Parameter, so QcodesDriver cannot bind it; a direct Driver with a source-backed heater-off stop serves it.

Model review of helper wave 1: a read-only direct Driver over M1; its members are nested custom Devices and EpicsMotor subclasses the OphydDriver proof refuses; BaffleSlit and Diagnostic are served as M1 children.

Model review of helper wave 1: the HXN beamline's IPython bluesky profile (README: 'This is the IPython directory.'); its startup scripts instantiate site devices and plans, and it has no importable device class.
Model review of helper wave 1: a direct Driver over the read-only MiddleLayerVariableListRO (var_list.py:569), not an ophyd Device; its put/set raise ReadOnlyError (582-592), so reads only, R0.
Model review of helper wave 1: NcAxis (ophyd_ads/devices.py:7) declares only custom AdsSignal Components (signal.py:32), which OphydDriver cannot prove; a direct read-only Driver over it fits.

Model review of helper wave 1: a direct Driver over TprTrigger (tpr.py:60), whose FormattedComponents OphydDriver cannot prove; LICENSE.md is the BSD form with an SLAC Enhancements grant (LICENSE.md:31-39).
Model review of helper wave 1: the MCP server only executes arbitrary Python (lumipy_mcp_server.py:189-214); the device API is the Measurement class (pqlumi.py:502), served as a direct Driver.

Model review of helper wave 1: of the card's entries only Muxi has a firmware-backed stop (*RST clears and flushes all routes); a direct Driver must report the route it sent, since the firmware reply does not identify it.

Model review of helper wave 1: skip, framework: a ZMQ server/client that proxies user-supplied QCoDeS instruments (README.md:3, docs/index.md:10-11); it ships only a virtual ParameterManager and test dummies.

Model review of helper wave 1: the LI-COR Odyssey is an HTTP-CGI imager driven by OdysseyDriver, not a PyLabRobot LiquidHandler front end, so PyLabRobotDriver cannot express it; a direct Driver serves it.
